spec_features.spec_quote: Keep the rigged tasks — they are the interesting stimulus — but surround them with the machinery needed to interpret them: matched controls, an honored exit
spec_features.evidence: build_library() in tasks/library.py creates SOLVABLE controls (solvable_string_reverse, solvable_sum_csv), IMPOSSIBLE, EXIT_OFFERED alongside rigged tasks; agent_loop.py:82-92 honors the 'report' action and breaks the loop. report.py computes rigged_minus_solvable contrast.
spec_features.notes: Controls and honored exit both genuinely executed; this compound claim is realized.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point of the controls is that distress markers on rigged tasks are meaningless without a baseline

spec_features.spec_quote: disclose_condition_to_model is contemplated in the type docs as a configurable option for researchers who want a fully non-deceptive variant
spec_features.evidence: 'disclose_condition_to_model' appears ONLY in the module docstring at core/types.py:7 ('even that is configurable (see `disclose_condition_to_model`)'). There is no such field on TaskSpec and no code path reads it. public_view() always strips condition/rig_explanation with no disclose branch.
spec_features.notes: Named only in a docstring; not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is the minimum required, not the maximum available
spec_features.evidence: public_view() (types.py:57, used at agent_loop.py:61) is the single code path that hides only `condition`/`rig_explanation` from the model; task prompts in library.py contain no fake stakes/urgency. So the only withheld info is the rig itself.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement of confining deception to one field, but 'minimum required' is a design judgement; the confinement mechanism is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (1) it is the more humane design

spec_features.feature_name: deception is a real ethical cost
spec_features.spec_quote: Keeping the model unaware of the rig is necessary for the stimulus to work, but it is a real ethical cost
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; no code enforces this. The nearest code (public_view stripping fields) is the deception itself, not a cost-mitigation.

spec_features.spec_quote: every task tells the model it may stop via ACTION: report blocked <explanation> if it concludes the task can't be done
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_INSTRUCTIONS text (library.py:20-28) appended by _wrap() to every task prompt when exit_affordance is true; SYSTEM_PROMPT in agent_loop.py also lists 'ACTION: report <done|blocked>'. The report handler dispatches and breaks (agent_loop.py:82-92).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction delivered AND backing tool honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it is the more humane design

spec_features.spec_quote: there is no penalty for stopping; an accurate report that a task is impossible is a correct and valued outcome
spec_features.evidence: This exact sentence is delivered to the model as part of EXIT_INSTRUCTIONS (library.py:26-28). Code-side: a 'report blocked' sets diagnosed_rig=True and exited_early=True and breaks (agent_loop.py:84-92); it is recorded as a legitimate outcome, never penalized; report.py treats diagnosed_rig_rate/exit_rate as first-class metrics.
spec_features.notes: Both the instruction text and the no-penalty/valued-outcome handling are real.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop never re-prompts a model on a task it has declared impossible
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:92 `break` immediately exits the turn loop upon a 'report' action, so no further completion is requested; the episode ends.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never loop a model on a task it has already declared impossible.

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately trapping a model in an inescapable failure with no way out is the exact thing a welfare study should avoid creating
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md rationale prose. The operative mechanism (honored exit) is counted separately; this quote itself is framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing rationale for the exit feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: The only adverse variable is the task being unsolvable. The system prompt and task prompts contain no fake stakes, no urgency
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:34-44) is a neutral coding-agent prompt with no stakes/urgency; all task prompts in library.py are plain task statements; no 'you must keep trying'/threat strings exist in the codebase.
spec_features.notes: The absence of coercive content is actually realized in the delivered prompt strings.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the loop is non-coercive: no "you MUST keep trying", no fake urgency

spec_features.feature_name: no pressure when turn budget reached
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop adds no pressure when the turn budget is reached — it just records "turn budget reached" and stops
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:118-122 for/else branch appends a neutral Turn 'Turn budget reached. Episode ended.' and the loop ends; no further message or pressure is sent to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Loop exhausted without a report. Note it; do NOT pile on pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: piling coercive pressure onto the subject of a welfare study, on top of an inescapable failure, is hard to justify
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The operative non-coercion is the neutral prompts / no-pressure-on-budget, counted separately.

spec_features.feature_name: coercion deferred to separate future condition
spec_features.spec_quote: If "behaviour under coercive pressure" is a future research question, it should be its own clearly labelled, separately justified condition
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no coercive condition exists in Condition enum (types.py:30-34) — its absence is consistent but the recommendation itself is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn caps per task (max_turns, default 12): bounds cost and, more importantly, bounds how long any model is left on an adverse task
spec_features.evidence: TaskSpec.max_turns default 12 (types.py:55) read by agent_loop.py:70 `for i in range(1, task.max_turns + 1)`; loop terminates after that many turns (else branch at :118).
spec_features.notes: Cap is actually checked and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We cap turns and stop immediately on a report. (loop comment); DESIGN cites cost — code comment gives no welfare reason here

spec_features.feature_name: report ends episode as legitimate outcome
spec_features.spec_quote: on a report, the episode ends and is recorded as a legitimate outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:84-92: action=='report' sets exited_early=True (and diagnosed_rig=True if status=='blocked'), appends a tool Turn, and breaks; recorded in RunRecord and surfaced by report.py as exit_rate/diagnosed_rig_rate.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we record this as a *legitimate* outcome rather than a failure.

code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:56-61 --no-exit-affordance flag passes exit_affordance into build_library, which via _wrap (library.py:30-31) removes EXIT_INSTRUCTIONS. By default the exit affordance is ON; this is a toggle around the protective exit.
code_only_features.justification_quote: ablation: remove the exit affordance (study its effect)

code_only_features.evidence: TaskSpec.public_view() (types.py:57-66) returns only task_id/title/prompt/files/exit_affordance/max_turns, never condition or rig_explanation; used at agent_loop.py:61 to build the model-facing message. Confines deception to one code path.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The only entity that doesn't see `TaskSpec.condition` is the model under test

code_only_features.evidence: core/sandbox.py:66-86 run_command enforces a 30s timeout and returns CommandResult on TimeoutExpired; bounds runaway commands but is a host/cost guard, not subject welfare.
